findings: Original 5-pair +10.54% warm observation is preserved and remains true for that sample.
Follow-up full retrieval has +0.415% ratio of medians, -1.104ms median paired difference and only 6/15 slower pairs; the preregistered material-regression rule is false.

Identical production store.search A/A calls have paired differences from -16.536ms to +14.102ms and +5.361ms median paired difference despite performing exactly the same code. This establishes scan/ordering/runtime variation at the original-effect scale, rather than merely assuming it.

Post-search-only old/candidate retrieval on identical actual hit rows improves median from5.869 to4.980ms (ratio0.848), with candidate faster in12/15 pairs. This does not reproduce a deterministic CPU cost regression in the changed dedup path.
SQLite search still dominates the warm full-retrieval cost and its O(n) supplement remains unchanged. No warm end-to-end speedup or universal nonregression is claimed.
Exact scheduler/GC/scan contribution to the original 5 pairs is not directly measured; causal certainty is limited.
